To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the canine model can be used to study the functional role of Ia molecules; 2) the guinea pig model may be useful for the same purpose, and 3) a single MAb reactive with HLA DR was found to be cross reactive with Ia molecules in several species.
14 of 16 murine anti-HLA-DR, DP, or DQ monoclonal antibodies reacted with peripheral blood monocytes from dogs, cats, guinea pigs, sheep, rabbits, and rats.

(1) MAb reactive with DR + DP molecules are more likely than those reactive with DR + DQ molecules to react with PBMC from a variety of animal species; (2) MAb that block canine MLC are generally reactive with PBMC from the guinea pig; (3) one MAb (H81.98.2) reactive with DR + PD molecules is highly conserved in nature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the reactivity and functional relevance of MAb in a variety of species.
the use of monoclonal antibodies to study the phylogenetic conservation of the HLA-DR molecule in nature.
the identification of Ia molecules in the dog, cat and rabbit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MAb reactive with the HLA-DR molecule are more likely than MAb reactive with DR + DP to react with non-human PBMC and to block MLC.
the reactivities of these MAbs in man and animals are not always parallel.
the canine MLC system is a valid model for the study of human HLA-DR and DR + DP molecules and that the guinea pig is a good model to study the function of human DR + DQ molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the guinea pig and cat are good models for studying the functional relevance of Ia molecules in humans, and the rabbit, dog, rat and sheep are not.
the guinea pig is the best model for studying the functional significance of Ia molecules, the sheep is a good model to study DR + DP molecules and the cat is the best model to study DR molecules.
the canine MLC can be inhibited with MAb recognizing HLA-DR or DR + DP molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the guinea pig is the best animal model to evaluate the functional role of specific Ia determinants in man.
the canine model may be useful to study the role of specific Ia antigens in the immune response.
the canine MLC is an excellent model to study Ia molecule function and that the guinea pig is an excellent model for studying Ia molecule function in the context of the mixed lymphocyte reaction.
